questions.question: In a fruit basket, the ratio of apples to oranges is the same as the ratio of limes to lemons. If there are 10 oranges, 9 limes, and 18 lemons, how many apples are there?

solution.exhibit_text:
The ratios are equal, so set up a proportion:

\[\dfrac{a}{10}=\dfrac{9}{18}\]

Cross multiply:

\[a\times18=9\times10\]
\[18a=90\]
\[a=5\]

questions.question:
During a hiking trip, a group of students recorded the elevation (in feet) at several points along the trail:

\[-95 \text{ ft}, 60 \text{ ft}, -40 \text{ ft}, 10 \text{ ft}, 75 \text{ ft}, -15 \text{ ft}\]

What is the difference between the highest and lowest elevations recorded on the trail?

Enter your answer in the space.

solution.exhibit_text:
The highest elevation is \(75\) ft (farthest right on a number line). The lowest elevation is \(-95\) ft (farthest left).

Subtract the lowest from the highest:

\[75-(-95)=75+95=170\text{ ft}\]

questions.question: In a showing of an artist's works, the ratio of the number of sculptures, sketches, and etchings shown is \(3{:}5{:}4\), respectively. If the number of sketches shown was 60, what is the total number of etchings and sculptures that were shown?

solution.exhibit_text:
The ratio of sculptures to sketches to etchings is \(3:5:4\). Since the number of sketches is 60, each ratio unit is multiplied by \(60\div5=12\).

Sculptures: \(3\times12=36\)
Etchings: \(4\times12=48\)

Add them: \(36+48=84\).

solution.exhibit_text:
The ratio of murals to collages to prints is \(3:5:4\). Since the number of collages is 30, each ratio unit is multiplied by \(30\div5=6\).

Murals: \(3\times6=18\)
Prints: \(4\times6=24\)

Add them: \(18+24=42\).

questions.question: For each \(\dfrac{2}{5}\) foot of curtain width, \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) yard of fabric is needed to make ruffles. How many yards of fabric are needed per foot of curtain width?

solution.exhibit_text:
It takes \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) yard of fabric for \(\dfrac{2}{5}\) foot of curtain width.

Find the ratio of 1 foot to \(\dfrac{2}{5}\) foot:

\[1\div\dfrac{2}{5}=\dfrac{5}{2}\]

Multiply by the fabric amount:

\[\dfrac{5}{2}\times\dfrac{3}{4}=\dfrac{15}{8}\text{ yd}\]

Multiply by the fabric amount:

\[\dfrac{8}{5}\times\dfrac{7}{10}=\dfrac{28}{25}\text{ yd}\]

A tablet screen is designed to be \(90\) millimeters wide. The quality control team allows for a variation of \(\pm5\%\) in the width. Select the minimum and maximum screen widths that fall within the acceptable range of screen widths, in millimeters.

The acceptable screen width is from [DROPDOWN_1] to [DROPDOWN_2] millimeters.

solution.exhibit_text:
The probability of winning a prize is \(\dfrac{1}{30}\). The probability of receiving Card C1 is \(\dfrac{1}{80}\).

questions.question: In a scale drawing of a triangular garden, the sides measure \(4\) inches, \(6\) inches, and \(9\) inches. The perimeter of the actual garden is \(38\) miles. What is the actual length of the shortest side of the garden?

The perimeter of the scale drawing is \(4+6+9=19\) inches.

The shortest side on the drawing is \(4\) inches, so its actual length is:

Which inequality represents this situation, where \(x\) is the number of hours Kayla can rent the bounce house?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) represent the number of hours. The hourly cost is \(20x\), and the one-time setup fee of $\(25\) is added to it.

\[25+20x\le150\]

The perimeter of square \(W\) is \dfrac{3}{2} times the perimeter of equilateral triangle \(X\). What is the ratio of the length of one side of square \(W\) to the length of one side of equilateral triangle \(X\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
The perimeter ratio of square to triangle is \dfrac{3}{2}\(:1\).

A square has \(4\) equal sides; a triangle has \(3\).

Side ratio: \(\dfrac{3}{2\times4}\Big/\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{3}{8}\times3=9:8\).
